newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end shortened session just off high.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end shortened session just off high.

text.p: Italian shares which opened at 1200 GMT after a four-hour delay due to a technical hitch closed just off the day's highs on Friday, boosted by subdued U.S. August CPI data which allayed fears of a need for a new Fed rate rise, traders said.

Stocks languishing in recent sessions gained sharply on widespread shortcovering. "It was a session which allowed us to get our breath back even if it might just be all down to a simple technical correction," one dealer said.
The All-share Mibtel index closed 1.97 percent up at 9,624 after late high of 9,630 while the Mib30 blue chip index ended up 2.49 percent at 14,400 after touching 14,424.

Troubled high-tech group Olivetti opened slightly firmer but slipped back 0.45 percent at the close to 572 lire, one of the few losers of the short trading day. "The share seems to be stabilising," one trader said. Olivetti, asked by bourse watchdog Consob on Thursday evening for more details on its accounts up to end-August, is due to meet analysts next week.

Compart, formerly Ferruzzi, soared 8.52 percent to 544 lire while sister company Montedison gained 3.83 percent to 965. Traders said gains were due to a statement Thursday that both companies expect "significant" first half net profit.
Food group Parmalat, buffeted in past days over a botulism scare, climbed 7.11 percent to 1,944 lire.
State-controlled energy group Eni rose 2.99 percent to 6,860 lire on news its Snam natural gas unit Snam signed a deal with Gasprom to export methane gas from Russia.

Mobile phone operator TIM fell 1.52 percent to 2,989 lire in heavy volume of nearly 18 million shares, still hit by worries over over the government's decision to hold a tender for Italy's third mobile phone licence this autumn which traders say is bound to attract big foreign interest.
Initial estimates saw fairly active trading of above 500 billion lire despite the restricted session.
